name: Spiritual Gifts and the Cessationist/Continuationist Question
path: Pneumatology: The Doctrine of the Holy Spirit

objectives.text: Identify that the Holy Spirit gives gifts to God's people
Name examples of spiritual gifts listed in Scripture such as teaching, serving, giving, and encouraging
Explain, using Paul's picture of the body, how each member's gift helps the whole church
Explain that the Spirit decides which gifts each believer receives and gives them for the common good
Plan and carry out a way to use an ability to serve classmates or the church as Peter commands
Explain from 1 Corinthians 13 why love is greater than any spiritual gift
Compare the gift lists in Romans 12, 1 Corinthians 12, Ephesians 4, and 1 Peter 4 by sorting the gifts into speaking, serving, and sign gifts
Explain how miraculous signs in the New Testament confirmed the message of Christ and his apostles
Explain how Paul's teaching on gifts corrects both pride and envy among believers
Describe how the ministry gifts of Ephesians 4 equip the saints for service and build up the church to maturity
Analyze the foundational and unrepeatable role of the apostles and prophets in the church
Define cessationism and continuationism and state the main question that divides them
Explain how the Westminster Confession connects the completion of Scripture to the cessationist argument
Compare major interpretations of when the perfect comes in 1 Corinthians 13
Explain the continuationist case for the ongoing exercise of all spiritual gifts
Analyze Paul's regulations for tongues and prophecy in public worship including interpretation, order, and edification
Evaluate abuses of spiritual gifts such as Corinthian disorder and prosperity claims using biblical criteria
Evaluate claims of authoritative new revelation against the Reformed teaching on the sufficiency of Scripture and the biblical tests for prophecy
Construct a reasoned position on the cessationist and continuationist debate that engages the key texts and confessions and represents the other view fairly
Propose practical ways for believers who differ on the gifts to maintain the unity of the Spirit in the body of Christ

changes: Replaced the invalid reference Jude 3 with Jude 1:3. Kept and reworded the real competencies: gifts given by the Spirit, examples, the body image, purpose, love over gifts, sign gifts, apostles and prophets, the perfect in 1 Corinthians 13, sufficiency of Scripture, the continuationist case, abuses, new revelation, constructing a position, and unity. Dropped the filler objective that only restated diversity of gifts. Turned the pride-focused application into a service practice students carry out and an explanation of how Paul corrects pride and envy. Added objectives on the confirming role of signs, Ephesians 4 equipping ministries, defining the two positions, worship regulations in 1 Corinthians 14, and tests for prophecy. Added confessional anchors in Westminster Confession of Faith 1.1, 1.6, and 26.1 and Heidelberg Catechism Q55.
